# About Us

Image: Boarding Icon

Since 1989, Cheshire Cat Feline Health Center has been dedicated exclusively to the health and well-being of cats in San Diego, CA, and the surrounding communities. As a full-service, feline-only veterinary hospital, we have cared for thousands of cats while building lasting relationships with the people who love them.

Everything we do is thoughtfully designed with your cat's comfort, health, and happiness in mind—from our calm, cat-friendly environment to the compassionate, personalized care we provide at every visit. We are committed not only to delivering exceptional veterinary medicine, but also to educating and supporting pet owners so they can make informed decisions throughout every stage of their cat's life.

We invite you to give us a call to learn more about our practice and discover how Cheshire Cat Feline Health Center can provide the specialized care your cherished kitty deserves.

## How To Save Money at Wicker Park Veterinary Clinic

#### Pet Insurance

Image: Veterinarian holding puppy

Like all veterinarians, Wicker Park Veterinary Clinic accepts pet insurance for unexpected accidents & illnesses. Find the best pet insurance in Illinois. Important: because pet insurance will not cover pre-existing conditions, it's important to get your pet insured while they're still healthy.

Get Pet Insurance

#### Wellness Plans

Image: Calendar

In addition to insuring against accidents & illnesses, some insurance providers offer routing care add-ons, or "wellness plans" that help you afford the cost of your pets routine health expenses.

Consider Wellness Plans

#### Treatment Financing

Image: Financing Solutions

Having pet insurance is the best way to avoid unexpected medical costs, but if you have expenses for existing medical conditions and need help financing the cost, ask your vet if they accept financing solutions like CareCredit and Scratchpay. These payment options will help you space out your payments over time, so you can afford any large unexpected upfront costs.

Evaluacion de un producto a base de aceite esencial de oregano sobre la integridad intestinal, la capacidad de absorcion de nutrientes y el comportamiento productivo de pollos de carne (https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03728)
citeturn285academia8 [wordlim: 200] Published: 4.6 years ago; 
Title: Evaluacion de un producto a base de aceite esencial de oregano sobre la integridad intestinal, la capacidad de absorcion de nutrientes y el comportamiento productivo de pollos de carne
Authors: Diego Martinez
Date: Thu Apr  7 20:42:43 2022

Eight experiments were conducted to test an oregano-essential-oil-based product (PRO) on performance, gut health, and nutrient absorption capacity in broilers. The first three, up to 14d and without specific challenges, tested the effects on intestinal histology, skeletal integrity, and growth. Other two experiments, up to 28d birds were challenged to induce feed passage syndrome (STR) and test the effect on the antioxidant status and performance, contrasting later the results under a natural challenge in commercial conditions. Finally, in two other experiments, up to 21 d, birds challenged with coccidia were tested to determine the effects on coccidiosis, nutrient digestibility, and feed efficiency (FCR). Corn-soybean-fish meal diets were used. Under healthy conditions, PRO effects were observed on intestinal villus height and surface area, mucosa density and structure, villus to crypt ratio, goblet cells density, mucus production, body weight gain, and FCR (P<0.04), and carcass yield and bone density (P<0.08). Birds affected by STR showed effects (P<0.05) on superoxide dismutase activity, bodyweight gain, FCRE, non-normal feces frequency, bursal diameter, and dysbacteriosis. Birds affected by coccidia showed effects on cocci-positive ratio, cocci microscopic score, oocysts count, bursal diameter, body weight gain, FCR, apparent digestibility of dry matter and crude protein, protein and energy efficiencies (P<0.01), and nitrogen apparent retention (P<0.07). Results showed PRO added value to the diet favoring feed efficiency and performance.
